history.period: Built over 13 years; mandir structure completed 1985; complex inaugurated 1992
history.summary: A 23-acre BAPS Swaminarayan temple complex in Gandhinagar, inspired by Yogiji Maharaj (1892-1971) and created by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The central Akshardham mandir is built from 6,000 metric tons of pink sandstone from Rajasthan (108 ft high, 131 ft wide, 240 ft long, 97 carved pillars, 17 domes), constructed with no steel or iron per Vedic architectural principles. Over 4,000 volunteers contributed ~8 million hours to the build. DATE CONFLICT (verify): Wikipedia gives completion/inauguration as 2 November 1992 (infobox) / 4 November 1992 (article body), while BAPS's own timeline says Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated it on 30 October 1992. On 24 September 2002 the complex was attacked by two Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists, killing 33 worshippers and wounding 70; the complex reopened 14 days later. The complex includes exhibition halls (Sahajanand Darshan, Neelkanth Darshan IMAX film, Sanskruti Vihar boat ride), the Abhishek Mandapam, Sahajanand Van gardens, a Premvati food court, and the Sat-Chit-Anand water-and-laser show after sunset.

name: BAPS Akshardham Temple, Gandhinagar
town_description: Gandhinagar is the capital of Gujarat and a planned city on the west bank of the Sabarmati river, about 25 km north of Ahmedabad. Laid out in a grid of numbered sectors with wide green avenues, it houses the Gujarat Vidhan Sabha and Secretariat, along with the Akshardham complex, the Children's Park, and Indroda Nature Park. It is Gujarat's administrative and institutional hub and a convenient base for temple tourism in north-central Gujarat.

travel.airport: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad, ~28 km (verify)
travel.road: On J Road, Sector 20, Gandhinagar; well connected by road to Ahmedabad (~25 km) and to northern Gujarat

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant winter); evenings combine darshan with the water show
visitor_information.opening_hours: Mandir darshan ~10:00 AM - 7:30 PM Tue-Sun; CLOSED every Monday; exhibitions ~10:30 AM - 5:30/6:00 PM; Sat-Chit-Anand water show after sunset ~7:30 PM; morning aarti ~10 AM, evening aarti ~6-6:30 PM (verify - sources differ between 9:30/10:00 AM opening); entry to mandir/gardens free, exhibitions and water show ticketed; mobile phones, cameras and electronics prohibited inside
